s.g: Used to form adjectives from nouns with the meaning “of or pertaining to”.
ex: Cyril + -ic → Cyrillic
acid + -ic → acidic

s.g: Used to denote certain chemical compounds in which a specified chemical element has a greater oxidation number than in the equivalent compound whose name ends in the suffix -ous. For example sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) has…
Forms nouns denoting the act or process whereby a subject becomes something else.
Forms transitive verbs meaning "to make" from adjectives and nouns.
Forms intransitive verbs meaning "to become" from adjectives and nouns.
Used to form nouns of action, process, or result based on the accompanying verb ending in -ise or -ize.
ex: baptism (1300), aphorism (1528), criticism (1607), magnetism (1616)

s.g: Used to form the name of a school of thought, system, or theory based on the name of its subject or object or alternatively on the name of its founder (When de-capitalized, these overlap with the generic "doctrines"…
ex: Lutheranism (1560), Calvinism (1570), Protestantism (1606), Congregationalism (1716), Mohammedanism (1815),: Palamism (1949)

s.g: Used to form names of a tendency of action, behaviour, condition, opinion, or state belonging to a class or group of persons, or the result of a doctrine, ideology, or principle or lack thereof.
Used to form countable nouns indicating a peculiarity or characteristic of language
ex: Atticism (1612), Gallicism (1656), archaism (1709), Americanism (1781), colloquialism (1834), newspaperism (1838), Shakespearianism (1886)

s.g: Used to form names of ideologies expressing belief in the superiority of a certain class within the concept expressed by the root word, or a pattern of behavior or a social norm that benefits members of the group…
ex: racism (1932), sexism (1936), classism (1971), speciesism (1975), heterosexism (1979), ableism (1981)

s.g: a person who studies or practices a particular discipline;
ex: botanist, one who studies plants
psychiatrist, one who practices psychiatry

s.g: a person who uses a device of some kind;
ex: violinist, one who plays a violin
cyclist, one who rides a (bi)cycle

s.g: one who engages in a particular type of activity;
ex: adventurist, one who takes risks or goes on adventures
artist, one who makes art

s.g: one who suffers from a specific condition or syndrome
ex: autist, egoist
Note, these are related to -isms: autism, egoism

s.g: Used to form nouns denoting followers or adherents of a specified person, idea, doctrine, movement, etc.
ex: Adamsite, Campbellite, Jacobite, laborite, Mansonite, Reaganite, Thatcherite

s.g: Used to form nouns denoting descendants of a specified historical person, especially a biblical figure.
ex: Cainite, Ephraimite, Hamite, Japhetite, Lamanite

s.g: Used to form demonyms.
Used to form nouns denoting rocks or minerals.
ex: andalusite, anorthosite, anthracite, erythrite, forsterite, graphite, hawleyite, titanite

s.g: Denoting diseases characterized by inflammation, itself often caused by an infection.
Used to form the names of various fictitious afflictions or diseases.
ex: What to Do About Senioritis: Make Your Senior Year Count, College Board. Accessed April 4, 2008.

s.g: Used to form an uncountable noun from an adjective; especially, to form the noun referring to the state, property, or quality of conforming to the adjective's description.
ex: absurd + -ity → absurdity (“the quality of being absurd or inconsistent with obvious truth, reason, or sound judgment”)
anonym(ous) + -ity → anonymity (“the quality or state of being anonymous”)

s.g: Used to form a countable noun from an adjective, referring to someone or something that conforms to the adjective's description.
ex: absurd + -ity → [an] absurdity (“that which is absurd; an absurd action; a logical contradiction”)
anonym(ous) + -ity → [an] anonymity (“that which is anonymous”)

s.g: Used to form other nouns, especially abstract nouns.
An adjective suffix signifying relating or belonging to, of the nature of, tending to, or serving to; as: affirmative, active, conclusive, corrective, diminutive.
Forms nouns denoting the act, process, or result of doing/making what is denoted by the noun/adjective.
to make what is denoted by the noun/adjective
ex: pixel + -ize → pixelize

s.g: to do what is denoted by the noun/adjective
ex: cannibal + -ize → cannibalize
